Emerson Workbench

A system for turning legacy training decks — and, increasingly, raw source manuals with no deck at all — into doing-centered courses for Emerson Educational Services. This page is a snapshot: architecture, current progress, and the reference docs, in one place to reground on or share.

§00

Mission

Why this exists, in three sentences.

Everything here ultimately serves the person on the other side of an instructor — the technician setting an actuator's travel, the operator diagnosing a failure. Training instructors well, including through IfE, is not the point; it's how that learner gets a class worth their time.

A class is the instructor and the hardware in the learner's hands — not a slide deck — because that's what actually builds a skill someone can use on the job. Success is measured by what a learner can do afterward, not what they can recite, so the curriculum is built from competencies and teaching primitives, not a legacy deck's chapter order.

The Workbench exists to make that kind of course buildable at scale, and to make sure the instructors carrying it into a room are ready to teach it well — with a real, provable pipeline, a shared source-of-truth library, and human judgment kept exactly where it belongs: on the editorial calls a machine shouldn't make alone.

Implementation tooling, kept out of the core shape above

Two real modules attach to this pipeline at specific points. They're utility tooling, not architecture — drawn separately here rather than in the diagram, so the five-stage shape stays legible.

Naming note: the Pipeline Console's own code is not in this vault — it's a separate repository that drives Claude Code with this vault as its working directory. Its diagram-cleanup.js module and this vault's 40 - Engine runtime are two genuinely different "engines" that happen to share a name.
§05

Component Index & Instructional Primitives, in numbers

The wiring above shows the mechanism; this is the scoreboard. A shared library, and per-course pointers into it — not two equal boxes.

144/144
Proof the shared-library asymmetry is real: the oil-and-gas sourcebook catalogue — 144 figures, 13 chapters, fully cited — is Component-Index-only. Zero primitive-registry entries. It sits in the shared library waiting for whichever future course needs one of its components.

Competency IDs are flat and location-independent (<domain>.<area>.<slug>, e.g. mnt.actuator.set-travel). Role — maint-tech / inst-tech / sizing-eng / operator — is a routing filter on which competencies a course points toward, never a depth dial, and never lives on a primitive itself.

Status: Phases 1–4 of the Instructional Primitives Pathway are complete (schema, ch3 retrofit, Day-One competency map, the 14101 primitive registry). Phase 5 — origination-mode Stage 1/2, cutting a module from objectives alone with no deck to read — has run one bounded dry run against ch3-m1, reviewed by Franz. A second origination trial is in progress in an isolated scratch clone, testing the oil-and-gas Component Index against the diagram-cleanup + lightbox pipeline (see the wiring diagram above).

§09

Flagged, not silently resolved

Named rather than quietly smoothed over while building this page.

→
curriculum-development.md's stale phase header.

Still reads "Phase 1 gate review" though the Pathway has reached Phase 5. Left untouched deliberately — Franz wants to update it himself, not have it bumped as a side effect. Logged in Open Questions.

→
Ch 3's course.json status vs. its real progress.

"outline" in the nav-facing field, but Stage 1–2 closed and Stage 3 under way in the Console's own project store. Logged in Open Questions, not corrected here.

→
Two unrelated "Phase" numbering schemes.

The Instructional Primitives Pathway's phases (currently 5) and the Pipeline Console's own build phases (0–6) both run similar ranges by coincidence. Kept visibly distinct in §01/§05 of this page and in System Map.md.

→
diagram-cleanup.js vs. 40 - Engine.

Same-sounding "engine," two different codebases (Console repo vs. vault runtime). Drawn as visibly separate, accent-marked nodes in the §01 wiring diagram rather than left to be conflated.

→
System Map's update protocol was never actually wired to anything.

No hook, no CI check, no Obsidian plugin — confirmed by checking .claude/settings.local.json (empty) and .obsidian/ (no community plugins). It's prose depending on someone remembering. The Log & Backlog below exists partly to not repeat this — see its closing note.

→
Two different "module objective" concepts, not yet reconciled.

Stage 2 of the pipeline authors its own per-module objective (the older, pre-existing system); the curriculum schema separately gives each competency a bloom verb. Both describe similar ground. Surfaced building the §01 content-modeling diagram; drawn as a flagged overlap there, not merged into one.
